blocks.text: KING OF JUDAH · TWO KINGDOMS
Jotham. Sixteen years in Jerusalem, after ruling for his leper father.
REIGNEDi
16 years c. 750–732 BC (dates vary)
CAPITAL
Jerusalem
HOUSE
House of David 11th of 20 in Judah
VERDICT
✓ Did right “And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD”
PROPHETS
Isaiah son of Amoz · Micah the Morasthite · Hosea
JUDAH (THE SOUTH): 20 RULERS REHOBOAM → ZEDEKIAH
ACCESSION
How Jotham came to power
While Uzziah was a leper, "Jotham the king's son was over the house, judging the people of the land". 2 Kings 15:5 2 Chronicles 26:21
SUCCESSION
The two kingdoms
THE VERDICT
How Scripture judges the reign
“And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD”
2 Kings 15:34 (KJV) →
“he did according to all that his father Uzziah had done”
2 Kings 15:34 (KJV) →
BUT ALSO
But also: "the high places were not removed". 2 Kings 15:35
Chronicles: "the people did yet corruptly"; and "Jotham became mighty, because he prepared his ways before the LORD his God". 2 Chronicles 27:2 2 Chronicles 27:6
CHRONICLES GIVES IT AS
“And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD”
2 Chronicles 27:2 (KJV) →
JUDAH (THE SOUTH): 20 RULERS
✓ Did right ✕ Did evil ◐ Mixed ● No verdict formula
THE KINGDOM
Jerusalem and the places of the reign
Judah (the south) · tribe of Judah. Only places Scripture names are shown, each where the Atlas puts it.
EVENTS
Wars, works and turning points
UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
THE NATION
What the nation did
The people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places. 2 Kings 15:35
"The people did yet corruptly" (Chronicles). 2 Chronicles 27:2
PROPHETS
Prophets of the reign
Is Isaiah son of Amoz His visions are dated in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah.
Mi Micah the Morasthite The word of the LORD came to him "in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah".
Ho Hosea Dated to the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah.
ON THE WORLD STAGE
The powers of the day
ARAM AND ISRAEL
Rezin · Pekah
TWO ACCOUNTS
Where Kings and Chronicles differ
Each ribbon joins the two accounts of one matter, passage to passage.
What each book adds
2 KINGS
2 CHRONICLES
A twentieth year
2 KINGS
2 KINGS · 2 CHRONICLES
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
16 years (2 Kgs 15:33). Scripture gives lengths and cross-dates, never BC years.
THIELE, REVISED BY MCFALL (1991)
Shared rule with Uzziah, 750–739 BC
Printed form: 739–732/731; co-regency from 750 (PDF p. 29).
YOUNG (2005), REVISING THIELE
Shared rule with Uzziah, 750–740 BC
Printed form: 740/739–732/731; co-regency from 750 (p. 246 (Table 2)).
ALBRIGHT (1945)
Shared rule with Uzziah, 750–742 BC
Printed form: c. 742–735; co-regency from c. 750 (p. 21).
TRADITIONAL DATES (USSHER, 1658)
Printed form: 758–742 (p. 59 (scan leaf n34)).
Counted from his co-regency
L. McFall (1991); R. C. Young (2005)

Jotham's years are counted from his co-regency, which began about 750 BC when his father became a leper; his twentieth year from then is 732/731, when Hoshea killed Pekah. 2 Kings 15:5 2 Kings 15:30 2 Kings 15:33 [117][130]
Counted on from Jotham's accession
James Ussher, followed by C. F. Keil (1872)
Ahaz has not yet been introduced at this point in Kings, so the year is counted on from Jotham's accession; it falls in Ahaz's fourth year. 2 Kings 15:30 2 Kings 16:1 [162]
A mistake in the numbers
J. R. Lumby (1887)

Since Jotham reigned sixteen years, there must be some mistake in the numbers here or in verse 33; no satisfactory solution is likely until the Assyrian and Egyptian annals are in order. 2 Kings 15:30 2 Kings 15:33 [163]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 6
2 Kings 15 2 Chronicles 26 2 Chronicles 27 Isaiah 1 Hosea 1 Micah 1
PASSAGES · 10
2 Kings 15:5 2 Kings 15:7 2 Kings 15:30 2 Kings 15:32–38 2 Chronicles 26:21 2 Chronicles 26:23 2 Chronicles 27:1–9 Isaiah 1:1 Hosea 1:1 Micah 1:1
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not say how long Jotham governed for his father before he became king.
No prophet is said to have spoken to Jotham directly.
